note: Read-only candidate contract for Zotero. This is reference data for the runtime owner, not a profile: no credential appears here, nothing is installed, and no packaged recipe exists. Every value is synthetic.

api_version.documented: Use of the Zotero-API-Version header is recommended for production code. API version 3 is currently the default and recommended version, and the response version is returned in the Zotero-API-Version response header.
api_version.note: Because v3 is the documented default, this header is a recommendation rather than a prerequisite. It is recorded so the runtime owner can support a pinned version later, and it is deliberately not counted as a capability gap for a first read.

supported_today.Authorization: Bearer <Zotero API key from the user keyring>
supported_today.documented: API keys can be included as Zotero-API-Key, as Authorization: Bearer, or as a ?key= query parameter, which the documentation marks not recommended. The bearer form is already what the recipe transport carries.

credential_derived_alternative.Zotero-API-Key: <Zotero API key from the user keyring>
credential_derived_alternative.documented: The Zotero-API-Key header is the documented first choice and is the form the identity documentation is written against.
credential_derived_alternative.note: Only needed for users who prefer the header form, and only because the documented identity route is written against it. It is a separate requirement from a static version header.

never.path: No credential may appear in a path or query. The documented ?key= form is not used.
never.documented: Use of an HTTP header is recommended, as it allows use of URLs returned from the API without modification.

identity_contract.documented: The syncing documentation uses GET /keys/current to verify key access and shows a response with userID, username and an access object.

documented_response_shape.access: object with user and groups permission flags in the documented example

limitations: No formal schema is documented, so field types and nullability are unverified. The username label is treated as required by example only.

The documentation describes this route as returning information about the key provided in the Zotero-API-Key header. Whether a key carried as Authorization: Bearer is accepted here is unverified, and that is exactly the one thing a framework test would have to prove first.
The documented example on the reference page is malformed, so only the field names are treated as evidence.
identity_contract.binding_requirement: The account's numeric userID appears in every library route, so identity has to hand that value to a later read path.

smallest_useful_read.documented: A specific item in a library is /users/<userID>/items/<itemKey>. Local object keys should conform to the pattern /[23456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ]{8}/, which the reviewed destination character set already accepts.

projected_fields.label: key
projected_fields.documented: Present in the documented item example.

projected_fields.label: version
projected_fields.documented: Present in the documented item example.

projected_fields.label: item_type
projected_fields.documented: Documented as a writable field, and all properties other than itemType, tags, collections and relations are optional.

projected_fields.label: date_added
projected_fields.documented: Present in the documented item data.

projected_fields.label: date_modified
projected_fields.documented: Present in the documented item data.

deliberately_not_projected.reason: Title is not documented as present for every item type. The documented note template has no title field, so projecting it would make a read fail for notes and attachments rather than describe them.

smallest_useful_read.no_schema_warning: No formal item schema or required-versus-optional table is documented, so every projected field is backed by the documented example or the documented write semantics rather than by a schema. A framework test should confirm each field against a real library before a profile relies on it.

listing.documented: A multi-object request returns a JSON array, and when results exceed the limit the API includes pagination links in the HTTP Link header with rel=first, prev, next and last.
listing.paging: limit (1-100, default 25) and start, plus a Link header and a Total-Results header

documented_statuses.403: Authentication errors such as an invalid API key or insufficient privileges return 403 Forbidden.
documented_statuses.404: An invalid request such as an unknown item returns 404 Not Found.
documented_statuses.429: The API may return 429 Too Many Requests, potentially with a Retry-After header, and clients should wait at least that many seconds or back off exponentially.
documented_statuses.503: Retry-After can also be included with 503 Service Unavailable during maintenance.

failure_document.note: The documentation states the statuses but does not document a JSON error envelope for single reads. A framework test should therefore assert status handling only, and must not depend on an error body field that no official reference documents.

rate_limit_headers.Backoff: May be included in any response, including successful ones, when the API servers are overloaded.
rate_limit_headers.Retry-After: Documented on 429 responses, and also on 503 during maintenance.

framework_gap.minimum_missing_behavior: Carry a value returned by the identity request, such as the numeric userID, into a later reviewed read path, so a single-item read does not have to pin the account's own id in source. Without that, no useful read exists, because every library route starts with /users/<userID> and no account-scoped alias is documented.
not_required_for_a_first_read: The Zotero-API-Version header, because v3 is the documented default.
The Zotero-API-Key header, because Authorization: Bearer is documented.
List paging, which only blocks listing.
framework_gap.not_a_gap: Nothing here requires weakening origin rules, adding a credential to a path, or bypassing a documented restriction.

local_alternative.documented: A local API also exists on http://localhost:23119, with its own key rules for writes.
local_alternative.note: A loopback origin is a separate capability and is not proposed here.

pinned_library_id_alternative.summary: A limited read-only subset can exist before identity-derived path binding exists, by having the user fix their own numeric library id in a reviewed source file, exactly as the GitHub template fixes an owner and repository.

shape.artifact: a user-owned template under connectors/recipes/templates/, never a packaged default
shape.reads: GET /users/<pinned numeric library id>/items/{destination} where the destination is the item key
shape.path_shape: one pinned segment plus one caller-supplied destination segment, which the reviewed path rules already allow
shape.writes: none; this queue proposes no Zotero write, because write revisions need their own acceptance

what_it_still_needs: Identity has to work with the credential form the user chose, which is the pending empirical question below.
Field projections have to be confirmed against a real library, because no item schema is published.

mismatch_disclosure.engine_fact: A pinned path segment is reviewed source, not a value the interpreter can compare with the identity subject. The interpreter re-checks identity against the stored account, but it does not verify that a number written in a path equals the account's own user id.
mismatch_disclosure.consequence: If the pinned id belongs to another library or account, the request is simply sent and the service answers on its own terms.
mismatch_disclosure.documented_statuses: An unknown item is documented as 404, and an invalid key or insufficient privileges as 403. What a malformed library id returns is not documented, so no status is promised here.
mismatch_disclosure.required_disclosure: The guide for such a template must say, in the source review text itself, that the numeric library id is user-supplied and unchecked, and that a mismatch appears only as the service's own error.

scope_disclosure.documented: The identity response carries an access object with user flags for library, files, notes and write, and group flags for library and write.
scope_disclosure.required_disclosure: A key without library read access cannot read items at all, so a live acceptance record should note the library flag that was granted, and no write permission is needed for a read-only subset.

pinned_library_id_alternative.note: This is recorded as an assessment, not as a shipped template. One sign-in with no user-supplied account numbers stays the default goal, and the pinned id is the interim route rather than the destination.

empirical_status.policy: Documentation proves what an endpoint offers. A framework test can only prove Steed's own behaviour against a documented shape. Neither can show that a provider accepts a credential or sends a field, so those stay pending until a real account is used.
settled_by_documentation: Authorization: Bearer with an API key is a documented way to authenticate, and the query form is documented as not recommended.
Zotero-API-Version is documented as recommended rather than required, with version 3 as the current default.
Library routes begin with /users/<userID> or /groups/<groupID>, and no account-scoped alias is documented anywhere in the reference.
A multi-object request returns a JSON array and paging uses limit, start and a Link header.
An invalid key or insufficient privileges is documented as 403, an unknown item as 404, and rate limiting as 429 with Retry-After.
